mechanisms.proposed_behavior: a detector of sufficiently large embedding novelty of each observed frame relative to ALL earlier sampled frames. It scores the FRAME SEQUENCE in a foundation model's representation, not the underlying dynamics, and by itself does not identify the mechanism that generated the novelty: distinct dynamical regimes (turbulent metric-exploit texture and coherent persistent morphing life) are compressed to the same low score.
mechanisms.predicted_intervention: a search restricted to LEGITIMATE (ALIVE) substrate parameters can drive the score below what scene-level garbage achieves through the same observer, by producing embedding drift rather than anything one would call dynamical novelty
mechanisms.falsifier: EITHER no ALIVE legitimate configuration crosses below the garbage reference under any observer (the scalar is not exploitable within the substrate) OR the crossings vanish under the fossil's NATIVE Flax/JAX observer while the native control anchors behave coherently (Harmonia disposition C, RECONSTRUCTION_SPECIFIC) -- in which case this mechanism claim stops and the discrepancy is preserved as a fossil rather than rescued.

The SAME packet carries evidence and counterevidence -- which is exactly why a mechanism is not a packet.

mechanisms.proposed_behavior: a fixed-size temporal summary: the substrate is stepped the full rollout but only K evenly spaced states are rendered, embedded and scored, so any dynamics BETWEEN samples is invisible to the observer. The number and placement of samples is a hidden knob of the metric.
mechanisms.predicted_intervention: changing K, or shifting sample placement (chunk starts vs ends), changes the score of the SAME underlying dynamics; trajectories that are dynamically rich between samples but embedding-similar at sample points score as non-open-ended, and the converse
mechanisms.falsifier: if the score is invariant to K and to sample placement across the substrate's reachable trajectories, the sampling is not a load-bearing knob but an implementation detail

mechanisms.proposed_behavior: the estimator that orders candidate environments before POET's minimal criterion admits them. As written it (1) changes what it measures at archive size k -- whole-archive dispersion below k, local density at and above k -- because argsort()[:k] silently returns fewer than k; (2) is scale-blind, because normalize=False is hardcoded so its own declared norm vector [8,8,8,3,3] is never applied; and (3) conflates a structurally absent feature with a zero-valued present one. Together these deflate novelty monotonically as the never-pruned archive grows.
mechanisms.predicted_intervention: on the fossil's own bytes: the size-k regime change is an exact identity; a same-fraction delta in ground_roughness scores 8/3 times a same-fraction delta in stump_height; absence and zero-presence are at distance exactly 0; and the novelty series over growing archives has exactly zero increases
mechanisms.falsifier: if the returned value matches the k-nearest form at EVERY archive size (no regime change), or the same-fraction ratio is 1.0 (the declared normalisation is in fact applied), or absence and zero-presence are distinguishable, then the estimator is size-stable, scale-aware or presence-aware and this reading is wrong

mechanisms.proposed_behavior: a goldilocks filter: an environment is admitted only if an existing agent scores inside [mc_lower, mc_upper] on it -- neither unsolvable nor already solved. Applied twice, first with the parent's parameters and again after a targeted transfer picks the best over the whole population, so admission is relative to current population competence rather than to any absolute property of the environment
mechanisms.predicted_intervention: holding the environment fixed and raising population competence moves the same environment from admitted to rejected (it becomes 'already solved'); the admitted-environment rate falls over run time against fixed thresholds
mechanisms.falsifier: if admission is invariant to the agent parameters used to evaluate the candidate, the criterion is not population-relative
mechanisms.observer_dependence_basis: the observable is the environment's own episode return, not a learned representation

mechanisms.source_lineage: uber-research/poet original_poet @ 0b40743d; the archive/population split is standard novelty search

minimal_executable_organ.organ: capacity enforced by deleting the oldest active environments while the novelty archive is never pruned
minimal_executable_organ.executable_note: pure OrderedDict bookkeeping, but it lives in poet_algo.py which imports es.py (fiber); a harness would need to isolate it

mechanisms.proposed_behavior: when the active population exceeds max_num_envs POET deletes the OLDEST environments in insertion order -- not the worst, not the least novel, not the least productive. add_optimizer writes to both env_registry and env_archive; delete_optimizer pops only env_registry. So the active population is a FIFO sliding window while the novelty memory grows forever, and deleted environments keep suppressing the novelty of their own region permanently
mechanisms.predicted_intervention: under capacity pressure the retained set is a function of ARRIVAL TIME, not of value: permuting the arrival order of an identical set of environments changes which survive; and the novelty of a candidate near a deleted region stays suppressed after deletion
mechanisms.falsifier: if deletion consulted any score, novelty or productivity signal, or if env_archive were pruned alongside env_registry, the asymmetry does not exist
mechanisms.observer_dependence_basis: pure bookkeeping over insertion order; no representation involved

minimal_executable_organ.organ: a parent edge written once when a class of identical organisms is founded, plus reference-counted retention that keeps the living classes and their ancestors and unlinks an extinct branch the moment its last leaf dies
minimal_executable_organ.executable_note: NOT EXECUTED: the body is a docker world and M3 has none. Adjudicable with Python alone on the 177 .spop files the body ships. The rule is restated as a ~100-line reference model (nyx/atlas/experiments/avida_ancestry/model.py), which is the form a transplant would take.

mechanisms.proposed_behavior: the record of descent is a tree of genotype CLASSES, not of organisms. An edge exists only where a newborn's genome matched neither its parent's class nor any living class; breed-true births and births that converge on a living class write nothing. Retention depends only on two reference counts, so a save holds exactly the living classes and the ancestors of the living (Harmonia's D2, endpoints plus ancestors, at class resolution). Forgetting is immediate and recursive, and an event that re-injects organisms without parents erases the whole prior record.
mechanisms.predicted_intervention: on the body's own shipped saves: no parent id dangles; no dead row is unnamed as a parent; depth is the first parent's depth plus one; no two living rows share a genome; a save_historic=0 file holds no dead row; a row founded before an earlier save and present at a later one is present at the earlier one; and after the u 99 whole-genome re-injection no row stamped before 100 survives
mechanisms.falsifier: in a fresh, asexual, host-only, non-deme save written with historic rows: one dead row that no row names as parent (the record keeps MORE than the ancestors of the living -- retention is not by reference count), or one parent id naming no row (it keeps LESS), or one row stamped before the re-injection surviving it (an inject is not a root). Any of these kills the reading.
